verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents a transfer-in flow. It covers the cost (at-cost, with transfer prices shown upfront) and remaining registration time (most transfers add one year from the current expiration date). It also gives troubleshooting for locks (clientTransferProhibited) and for transfers that stall past the expected time frame. However, the EPP/auth-code step is never described, and status tracking appears only as troubleshooting guidance. Community reports are mixed: one user found transfers from GoDaddy smooth, while two others report duplicate charges and an expiration date not reflecting payment. These are isolated anecdotes rather than a documented contradiction, so they lower confidence rather than make the claim disputed. Missing for 10: explicit EPP/auth-code instructions, a documented transfer status-tracking view, and independent corroboration that the expiration date and billing are handled correctly.

support.subject: As a power user, transferring domains IN is documented and honest — EPP/auth-code flow, status tracking, what the transfer costs, and what happens to remaining registration time

citations.quote: Transferring a domain moves your registration from your current registrar to Cloudflare... Most transfers include a one-year extension from your current expiration date.
See registration, transfer, and renewal prices upfront, with no hidden fees or required add-ons.
If clientTransferProhibited appears in your domain WHOIS or RDAP output, the domain is still locked. Unlock it at your current registrar.
If your transfer has not been completed within that time frame, something has likely gone wrong.
